text:
jordyn: CI nightly just turned red on runtime unit tests — intermittent failure in ServeBackoffTest.test_retry_order. Happening on linux/mac, not sure if it's infra or test flake. anyone on?
ci-bot: CI job failed: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/5601234567 — test exit code 1, attached logs and stack.
sam: re-ran the same job 3x, failed 2/3 times with same assertion. quick log snippet:
```
E serve/backoff_test.cc:142: expected retries in chronological order
  observed: [retry2, retry1, retry3]
  expected: [retry1, retry2, retry3]
```
lucas: hm — sounds like wake ordering. Is the test using real timers or the fake scheduler?
elaine: it's using real timers + std::chrono. hypothesis: under high concurrency the timer wake order can be nondet. try setting `RUNTIME_TEST_SCHEDULER=fake` or running with `--shuffle-seed=0` to reduce nondet. also try `--test-repeat=100` to surface frequency.
sam: can someone kick a bisect across the commit window where this started? I can run local bisect if you give me the commit range.
jordyn: failing assertion and stack from CI: 
```
AssertionError: expected chronological order
at serve/backoff_test.cc:142
#0 0x7fabc runtime::Timer::fire()
#1 0x7fabd runtime::Scheduler::run_one()
#2 0x7fabe ServeBackoffTest::test_retry_order()
```
ci-bot: Artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/5601234567/log.txt (30MB)
lucas: quick workaround to reduce noise: add `std::this_thread::sleep_for(1ms)` at test startup to de-synchronize timer wakes — not ideal but useful to triage. Prefer fixing scheduler ordering.
elaine: if bisect shows it regressed after a kernel/timer-related change, we should add deterministic scheduler option to the test harness. I can draft a small PR that adds `--deterministic-timers` (env `TEST_DETERMINISTIC_TIMERS=1`) and a `TEST_RAND_SEED` to make order reproducible. @lucas @sam can you review when I open it?
sam: yes I'll review. also can someone run `tools/local-race-repro --target serve_backoff --repeat 200` on a mac runner (this seems higher on mac).
jordyn: starting bisect now across commits 6f3c..b7a9 — will post results or a pointer to a failed commit within ~30m. thanks for the quick ideas :coffee:
